purpose: Pin how the three required LK product frontends consume official company assets and product-shell identity, keep parent-brand-first ProductLockup output on an LDS-approved outlined registry instead of a free-form text API, and make name-approval and downstream migration gaps explicit.

designSystemOwns: approved positive, reverse, monochrome, square, inline, stacked, banner, and corporate outputs
brand colors, clear space, and minimum rendered sizes
the approved ProductLockup key registry and its frozen SemiBold 600 outlined LK-plus-product paths
ProductLockup parent-brand-first hierarchy, layout, positive and reverse appearance mapping, minimum size, and accessible-name structure
deterministic source hashes and platform export contracts
productOwns: proposal and approval of the canonical short product lockup name before LDS registration
whether TopBar or SideNav is the single product-lockup owner
the explicit full-lockup-to-mark breakpoint and optional tooltip composition

reviews.finding: The product repeats a product-local 264 by 233 gradient PNG rather than the canonical outlined LK assets. The four call sites meet or exceed the intended rendered-size floor but the artwork, color treatment, and source provenance are outside the brand contract. No Web Viz ProductLockup key is approved, so the migration cannot substitute arbitrary live text.

replacement.requiredProductAction: Propose and approve a canonical short lockup name, then request an LDS outlined-path registry entry before using a full product lockup.
replacement.lockupNameDecision: Web Viz is not an approved ProductLockup key. It may remain ordinary product-owned UI copy beside an interim mark, but LDS must not outline or register it until the product naming decision is approved.

sourceEvidence.note: 264 by 233 transparent PNG containing a blue gradient LK symbol.

reviews.finding: Navigation uses an independently stored square logo-light.svg and authentication uses favicon.ico. Both are large enough for the intended slots, but neither is tied to the current construction manifest or generator, so product and LDS geometry can drift. No Control ProductLockup key or canonical short lockup name is approved.

replacement.requiredProductAction: Propose and approve a canonical short lockup name, then request an LDS outlined-path registry entry before using a full product lockup.
replacement.navigationDecision: Until a Control key is registered, use the approved LK mark for a collapsed rail and do not synthesize a full LK-plus-name lockup. If the product intentionally retains a standalone official-square asset, the observed 55px slot remains below its 64px minimum.
replacement.lockupNameDecision: 로봇 관제 시스템 remains product-owned UI copy, not an approved outlined lockup name. The product must approve a canonical short lockup name before LDS can register its paths.

sourceEvidence.note: Loads /logo-light.svg with a default 55 by 55 slot.

reviews.finding: LK Portal's pinned sidebar already composes the LDS Lockup mark at a 20px rendered SVG height with a visible Portal label. Its composition is compatible, but the new ProductLockup proposal changes the product outline from the legacy ExtraBold 800 asset to parent-brand-first SemiBold 600, so Portal requires an explicit visual review as part of the package upgrade.

replacement.packageAction: Review the SemiBold 600 Portal proposal, then upgrade @lk-design-system/lds-theme from the pinned rc.23 artifact to a release containing ProductLockup constructionVersion 2, brand constructionVersion 4, and geometryVersion 1.0.
replacement.lockupNameDecision: The portal key resolves only to the approved parent-brand-first SemiBold outlined paths. The legacy ExtraBold 800 Lockup variant remains a separate compatibility and comparison asset; neither API accepts arbitrary product-name text.
